'''Hugh Norman Ross''' (born July 24, 1945) is a Canadian astrophysicist, [[Christian apologetics|Christian apologist]], and [[Old Earth creationism|old-Earth creationist]].

Ross obtained his [[Ph.D.]] in astronomy from the [[University of Toronto]]<ref>{{cite book |last=Utter |first=Glenn |date=August 1, 2001 |title=The Religious Right, 2nd Edition |url=https://archive.org/details/religiousrightre00utte_0/page/111 |publisher=ABC-Clio Inc |isbn=978-1576072127 |page=[https://archive.org/details/religiousrightre00utte_0/page/111 111] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.astro.utoronto.ca/theses/theses30-96.html|title=U of Toronto Astronomy Department Theses 1930-1996|website=www.astro.utoronto.ca}}</ref> and his [[B.Sc.]] degree in physics from the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.reasons.org/about/who-we-are/hugh-ross | title=Reasons to Believe - About -Who We Are | publisher=[[Reasons to Believe]] |date=2012  | access-date =2012-05-18 }}</ref> He established his own [[Christian ministry|ministry]] in 1986, called [[Reasons to Believe]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.reasons.org/articles/summary-of-reasons-to-believe-s-testable-creation-model | title= Summary of Reasons To Believe's Testable Creation Model |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201165407/https://reasons.org/articles/summary-of-reasons-to-believe-s-testable-creation-model|archive-date=2016-02-01 | author=Hugh Ross }}</ref><!--doesn't say it's by Ross<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.reasons.org/articles/creation-vs.-evolution-why-a-model-is-essential | title= Creation vs. Evolution: Why a Model Is Essential | author=Fazale Rana}}</ref>-->

Ross rejects both [[abiogenesis]] and [[evolution]] as explanations for the origin and entire history of life, contrary to the [[Level of support for evolution|scientific consensus]].<ref>{{Cite web  |date=2009-07-09 |title=Section 5: Evolution, Climate Change and Other Issues |url=https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2009/07/09/section-5-evolution-climate-change-and-other-issues/ |access-date=2022-07-28 |website=Pew Research Center - U.S. Politics & Policy |language=en-US}}</ref> Ross' position overlaps with that of [[intelligent design]], but Ross argues that the evidence points to Jesus Christ as the designer, instead of an undefined intelligent designer.<ref name="ID" /><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.reasons.org/articles/a-beginner-s-and-expert-s-guide-to-the-big-bang-sifting-facts-from-fictions | title= A Beginner's-and Expert's-Guide to the Big Bang: Sifting Facts from Fictions | author=Hugh Ross}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{cite web | url=https://reasons.org/explore/publications/articles/more-than-intelligent-design | title= More Than Intelligent Design | author=Hugh Ross}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Hugh Ross was born in [[Montreal]], Quebec, and raised in [[Vancouver]], British Columbia, after moving there at the age of five.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=100 Huntley Street: September 20, 2022 |url=https://www.100huntley.com/watch?videoID=338940 |access-date=2023-02-23 |website=www.100huntley.com}}</ref>  His parents were James Stewart Alexander Ross and Dorothy Isabel (Murray) Ross. He was interested in science from a young age, often reading science textbooks as a child.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Butcher |first=Andy |date=2003-06-01 |title=He Sees God in the Stars - Charisma Magazine |url=https://charismamag.com/charisma-archive/he-sees-god-in-the-stars/ |access-date=2023-02-23 |language=en-US}}</ref>

As a teenager, Ross read works by philosophers such as Immanuel Kant and Rene Descartes, but felt their works contained inconsistencies and contradictions.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=The happy warrior |url=https://wng.org/articles/the-happy-warrior-1617331435 |access-date=2023-02-23 |website=WORLD |language=en}}</ref> Ross also read Eastern holy books from religions such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Zoroastrianism.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> He began studying the Bible in secret due to his family's disapproval. He was inspired by the way the Bible described historical and scientific information, eventually becoming a Christian.<ref name=":1" /> 

Ross described his upbringing as moral, but not religious.<ref name=":0" /> Ross became interested in astronomy at the age of seven, after asking his parents whether stars were hot when gazing up at the night sky. He visited the local library to find the answer.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=My Story: Dr. Hugh Ross {{!}} Cru |url=https://www.cru.org/us/en/how-to-know-god/my-story-a-life-changed/hugh-ross.html |access-date=2023-02-23 |website=Cru.org |language=en-us}}</ref> He soon became convinced that the [[expansion of the universe]] and the [[The Big Bang|Big Bang]] required a divine "cosmic beginner".<ref name=":3" /> At 17 he began to serve as director of observations for Vancouver's [[Royal Astronomical Society]] and started examining religious texts.<ref name=":3" />

Ross received a provincial scholarship and a National Research Council of Canada fellowship and earned a [[B.Sc.]] in [[physics]] from the [[University of British Columbia]] in 1967,<ref name=":3" /> going on to earn a [[M.Sc.]] in 1968, and a Ph.D. in [[astronomy]] from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1973.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1973JRASC..67..200M Page 200 |url=https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1973JRASC..67..200M?utm |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=adsabs.harvard.edu}}</ref> While in Toronto, Ross began meeting with his fellow Christian students to share their faith.<ref name=":3" />

The National Research Council of Canada sent Ross to [[Caltech]] as a [[postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research fellow]] to study [[quasar]]s and [[galaxy|galaxies]] from 1973 to 1978.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hugh Ross |url=https://reasons.org/team/hugh-ross |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=Reasons to Believe |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ross |first=Dr Hugh |title=My Story: Dr. Hugh Ross {{!}} Cru |url=https://www.cru.org/us/en/how-to-know-god/my-story-a-life-changed/hugh-ross.html |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=Cru.org |language=en}}</ref> While at Caltech Ross met astronomer Dave Rogstad and joined his Bible study group, which included his future wife, Kathleen Ann Drake.<ref name=":3" /> The group encouraged him to spread his personal story about scientific evidence and Christianity.<ref name=":3" />
[[File:Hugh Ross presenting.jpg|alt=Ross presents at Grace Church St. Louis in November 2022|thumb|Ross presents at Grace Church St. Louis in November 2022]]

==Career==
Ross served as a minister of evangelism at [[Sierra Madre Congregational Church]]. He was encouraged by leaders in his church to start his own ministry,<ref name=":1" /> and in 1986 he and Kathy Ross founded the apologetics ministry ''Reasons To Believe'' in Sierra Madre, California.<ref name=":3" />

In 1989, Ross' first book on Christian apologetics was released, with sales exceeding a quarter million copies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Butcher |first=Andy |date=2003-06-01 |title=He Sees God in the Stars |url=https://mycharisma.com/charisma-archive/he-sees-god-in-the-stars/ |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=Charisma Magazine Online |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2012, Ross won the [[Trotter Prize (Texas A&M)|Trotter Prize]], delivering the Trotter Lecture at [[Texas A&M University]] on "Theistic Implications for Big Bang Cosmology."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-04 |title=Trotter Lecture Series - Texas A&M College of Science |url=https://science.tamu.edu/events/trotter/ |access-date=2023-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220404190428/https://science.tamu.edu/events/trotter/ |archive-date=2022-04-04 }}</ref>

Ross has made radio and television appearances, and his work has been covered by news outlets including Christianity Today,<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Neal |first=Sam |title=Bookmark: Creation as Science |url=https://www.christianitytoday.com/ct/2007/april/35.89.html |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=ChristianityToday.com |date=12 April 2007 |language=en}}</ref> The Houston Chronicle,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Quick |first=Mark |date=2003-07-22 |title=Intelligent Design model deserves equal class time |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/neighborhood/article/Intelligent-Design-model-deserves-equal-class-time-9837622.php |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=Houston Chronicle |language=en-US}}</ref> The LA Times,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lobdell |first=William |date=2001-06-23 |title=Seeing Faith Through Science |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2001-jun-23-me-13847-story.html |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> The Washington Post,<ref>{{Cite news |title=For some, eclipse day showcases God's majesty. For others, it means the Rapture is coming. |language=en-US |newspaper=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/acts-of-faith/wp/2017/03/15/the-first-solar-eclipse-to-cross-america-in-99-years-is-coming-to-some-its-an-act-of-god/ |access-date=2023-02-24 |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> Fox News,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-08-08 |title=Could 'mysterious radio signals' prove the existence of God? {{!}} Fox News Video |url=https://www.foxnews.com/video/5819662243001 |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=Fox News |language=en-US}}</ref> and CBN.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Astrophysicist Explains How God Is Not Constrained By Time or Space |url=https://cbn.com/article/bible-says/astrophysicist-explains-how-god-not-constrained-time-or-space |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=CBN |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2022, Ross stepped down as CEO of Reasons to Believe to focus his efforts on research, writing and other endeavors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Reasons to Believe Names Successor |url=https://reasons.org/explore/publications/news/future |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=Reasons to Believe |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Beliefs ==
Ross believes God has revealed his existence and divine nature through both the Bible and creation.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Hugh |title=The creator and the cosmos: how the latest scientific discoveries reveal God |date=2018 |isbn=978-1-886653-14-6 |edition=Fourth |location=Covina, CA |oclc=1034740438}}</ref> He also believes that his creation model is empirically testable, and equally plausible as the evolutionary model.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Hugh |title=More than a theory: revealing a testable model forcreation |date=2012 |publisher=Baker Books |isbn=978-0-8010-1442-0 |edition=Paperback |location=Grand Rapids, Michigan |oclc=794541436}}</ref> Ross also believes that the Earth is fine-tuned for life,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Hugh |title=Designed to the core |date=2022 |isbn=978-1-956112-01-6 |location=Covina, CA |oclc=1350647516}}</ref> and that science and Christianity intersect rather than contradict each other.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Hugh |title=Navigating Genesis: a scientist's journey through Genesis 1-11 |date=2014 |isbn=978-1-886653-86-3 |location=Covina, CA |oclc=861521932}}</ref> Ross believes that God has created the universe for several reasons and desires a relationship with humans.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Hugh |title=Why the universe is the way it is |date=2008 |isbn=978-0-8010-1304-1 |location=Grand Rapids, Mich. |oclc=216937304}}</ref>

Ross believes the record of nature is "like the 67th book of the Bible." He attempts to use science to find common ground with people, including secular scientists who reject the idea of God.

===Old-Earth Creationism ===
Ross believes in [[progressive creationism]], a view which holds that while the Earth is billions of years old, life did not appear by natural forces alone but that a [[supernatural]] agent formed different lifeforms in incremental (progressive) stages, and [[day-age creationism]], a system of reconciling a literal Genesis account of creation with modern scientific theories on the [[age of the universe]], the Earth, life, and humans.<ref name=":6">{{cite book| last = Pennock| first = Robert T.  | author-link = Robert T. Pennock| title = Tower of Babel, The Evidence against the New Creationism| publisher = The MIT Press| date = February 28, 2000|isbn = 0-262-66111-X| page = 20}}</ref> He rejects the [[Young Earth Creationism|young-Earth creationist]] positions that the earth is younger than 10,000 years and that the creation "days" of Genesis 1 represent 24-hour periods. Ross instead asserts that these days (translated from the Hebrew word ''[[yom]]''<ref name=":7">{{cite web| url=http://www.studylight.org/lex/heb/view.cgi?number=03117 |title=Yowm |website=StudyLight | access-date=2006-10-18}}</ref>) are historic, distinct, and sequential, but not 24 hours in length nor equal in length. Ross agrees with the scientific community that any version of [[intelligent design]] is inadequate if it does not provide a testable [[hypothesis]] which can make verifiable and falsifiable predictions, and if not, it should not be taught in the classroom as science.<ref name="MoreThanID">{{cite web | url=http://www.reasons.org/resources/fff/2002issue10/index.shtml#more_than_id|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011225836/http://reasons.org/resources/fff/2002issue10/index.shtml#more_than_id | author=Hugh Ross | title= More Than Intelligent Design | work=Facts for Faith, Issue 10 | access-date=2015-03-23|archive-date=2007-10-11}}</ref><ref name="ID">{{cite web | url=https://www.reasons.org/articles/more-than-intelligent-design-2 |publisher=Reasons To Believe | title=Creation Scientists Applaud PA Judge's Ruling Against 'Intelligent Design'-Dressing Up ID Is No Substitute for Real Science|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071008233814/http://www.reasons.org/resources/in_the_news/20051220.shtml|archive-date=2007-10-08 | access-date=2007-09-25}}</ref>

Ross has critiqued young-Earth creationists, in particular Russell Humphreys,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Russell Humphreys Responds to Criticism of His Book |url=https://www.icr.org/article/dr-russell-humphreys-responds-criticism-his-book |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=www.icr.org |language=en}}</ref> [[Ken Ham]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ross |first=Hugh |date=2022-09-26 |title=The Unintended Ham-Ross "Debate" |url=https://reasons.org/explore/blogs/todays-new-reason-to-believe/the-unintended-ham-ross-debate |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=Reasons to Believe |language=en-US}}</ref> and Henry Morris.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Days Do Matter |url=https://www.icr.org/article/479/ |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=www.icr.org |language=en}}</ref> He was influential in chemistry Nobel Laureate [[Richard Smalley]] becoming a Christian and spoke at his funeral.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Funeral Service for Professor Richard Smalley |url=https://jesusandscience.org/podcast/funeral-service-for-professor-richard-smalley-3/ |access-date=2025-09-30 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ross married Kathy in 1977 and they have two sons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kathy Ross |url=https://reasons.org/team/kathy-ross |website=Reasons to Believe}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

Kathy was formerly the senior vice president of Reasons to Believe and oversaw the organization’s communications.<ref name=":1" />

Ross has been diagnosed with [[Asperger syndrome]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Michalski |first=Daniel |date=2019-07-30 |title=The Gift of Autism |url=https://servantsofgrace.org/the-gift-of-autism/ |access-date=2023-02-25 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
